O instrumental: a «extensão do corpo»: The instrumental: the "extension of the body"
Uma cena que você já viveu (ou vai viver: Picture a scene you will probably live. You are in Russia and you want to say that you write with a pen. You think: "pen in Russian is ру́чка, and 'with' is с, so I will say я пишу́ с ру́чкой." The person gives you a puzzled look and corrects you: — Я пишу́ ру́чкой. You stare. It is the same word, ру́чка, but now it is in the instrumental (ру́чкой) and you did not use с. You wonder: "But I wanted to say with the pen! Why no с?" And the person explains: — Because the pen does not go along with you. The pen is part of you when you write. The pen is the extension of your hand. That is the doorway into the instrumental case, and it shows a beauty that English hides. Pay attention: after this lesson you will understand one of the biggest differences between the two languages. The little secret: the extension of the body. In English, the word "with" has two completely different senses that we never notice. Sense 1, instrument (the thing is an extension of your body): I write with a pen. I eat soup with a spoon. I cut bread with a knife. I paint with a brush. Sense 2, company (the thing is another person, not an extension): I go with you. I live with my mother. I talk with the teacher. I work with my colleagues. English uses the same word "with" for both, automatically. Nobody thinks about it. In Russian this is impossible: the two "with" are different structures. Sense 1 (instrument) = the bare instrumental, with no preposition. Sense 2 (company) = С + instrumental. See for yourself. Notice: in the first case the pen and the spoon are extensions of the body. You write, and the pen is part of the movement of your hand. You eat, and the spoon is part of the movement of your hand. The thing does not go with you; at that moment it is you. In the second case you and the other person are two separate beings. You go, and they go. You live, and they live. That is company, so it needs с.
O segredinho: a extensão do corpo: The little secret: the extension of the body
I eat soup with a spoon.
A metáfora do pintor. Vou te dar uma met: The painter metaphor. Here is a metaphor worth the whole lesson. Imagine Da Vinci without a brush. How would he paint the Mona Lisa? He would not. The brush is an extension of his hand. Without it his hand cannot do the action of painting. The brush is part of Da Vinci at the moment of painting. In Russian, Da Vinci painted ки́стью (a brush: bare instrumental), not с ки́стью, because the brush was not a companion. It was an extension of his hand. Another example: you eat soup. Without a spoon you cannot eat soup (unless you lift the bowl, but that is another matter). The spoon is the extension of your hand at the moment of eating. So in Russian you eat soup ло́жкой (bare instrumental), not с ло́жкой. Third example: you write a letter. Without a pen you cannot write. The pen is the extension of your hand at the moment of writing. So you write ру́чкой, not с ру́чкой. Now compare with company: you go to the cinema. You go, and your friend goes. Your friend is not an extension of your body. Your friend is another person, with their own will, their own feet, their own path. So you go с дру́гом (with the friend: С + instrumental). That is all. The rule is one question: is the thing an extension of your body? YES = bare instrumental (ру́чкой, ло́жкой, ки́стью). NO (it is another person or an independent thing) = С + instrumental (с дру́гом, с ма́мой). The magic question solves about 90% of cases. Here is how you decide between the bare instrumental and С + instrumental.
A pergunta mágica: a coisa é extensão do: The magic question: is the thing an extension of the body?

As 6 preposições do instrumental. Além d: The 6 prepositions of the instrumental. The instrumental is governed by 6 main prepositions: «с» (company) and five that express position. All of them express an idea of position or relation. One big rule: the change always comes AFTER the preposition. The preposition itself never changes; it is fixed. What changes is the word that follows it: the noun goes into the instrumental. Look at the examples. Notice that the preposition (над, под, пе́ред, ме́жду, за, с) is always the same, and it is the noun that takes the instrumental ending. That is why we say the preposition "governs" the instrumental: it demands that the word after it be in that case.
пе́ред до́мом (em frente da casa): пе́ред до́мом (in front of the house)
ме́жду столо́м и дива́ном (entre a mesa: ме́жду столо́м и дива́ном (between the table and the sofa)
стол virou столо́м, диван virou дива́ном: стол turned into столо́м, диван turned into дива́ном
O instrumental responde a «кем? чем?». E: The instrumental answers «кем? чем?». In English we use "with" and "by means of". Singular: hard masculine: -ом (брат → братом); soft masculine (-й, -ь): -ем (учитель → учителем, музей → музеем). After ж, ч, ш, щ and ц: -ем if the ending is unstressed (муж → мужем) and -ом if it is stressed (врач → врачом). Feminine: -а → -ой (мама → мамой); -я → -ей (неделя → неделей); -ь → -ью (ночь → ночью, дочь → дочерью). Neuter: -о → -ом (окно → окном); -е → -ем (море → морем). Plural, all genders: -ами or -ями (книги → книгами, студенты → студентами). Irregular: друзья → друзьями, дети → детьми, люди → людьми.
em português «com meu irmão» não muda a: in English "with my brother" does not change the word "brother". In Russian the noun itself changes: «с братом».

A distinção crucial: lugar (instrumental: The crucial distinction: place (instrumental) vs. movement (accusative)

The crucial distinction: place (instrumental) vs. movement (accusative). Here is a trap that catches almost every learner. The prepositions ПОД and ЗА change case according to the meaning: Place (rest) = instrumental. Movement = accusative. Look. The rule: place (where it is) = instrumental; movement (where it goes) = accusative. English hides this because "under the table" is the same whether the cat is lying there or running there. It is the same logic you already saw with В and НА in lesson 16 (where = prepositional; where to = accusative). Here: where = instrumental; where to = accusative. Two prepositions in this group never change: НАД (above) and ПЕ́РЕД (in front of) always take the instrumental, and МЕ́ЖДУ (between) normally does too. So the trap is really about ПОД and ЗА. Compare with В and НА (lesson 16). Notice: the accusative is always the case of movement. The case of rest changes: prepositional with В/НА, instrumental with ПОД/ЗА.
The cat is under the table.
The cat runs under the table.
The picture is above the table.
He hangs the picture above the table.
The house is behind the garden.
Terminações e tabela mestra do instrumen: Endings and master table of the instrumental
A regra da tesourinha do instrumental. A: The instrumental method. Now the endings. The method is the same as always: STEP 1: find the nominative form (the dictionary form). STEP 2: add the instrumental ending, which depends on the gender. STEP 3: done, the noun is in the instrumental. Notice: masculine and neuter get -ОМ/-ЕМ. Feminine in -а/-я gets -ОЙ/-ЕЙ (or the older, poetic -ОЮ/-ЕЮ). Feminine in -ь gets -ЬЮ. Neuter in -мя gets -ЕНЕМ. The big difference from the other cases: masculine and neuter both get -ОМ/-ЕМ (not -У, not -Е). It is a single ending. Then comes the master table of the instrumental. Watch the spelling rule: after the letters ж, ч, ш, щ, ц, an unstressed -ОМ/-ОЙ is written -ЕМ/-ЕЙ: това́рищ → това́рищем (not "това́рищом"); врач → врачо́м (stressed, so it stays -ом); муж → му́жем (not "мужом"); ноша → но́шей.
A tabela mestra do instrumental: The master table of the instrumental
A preposição с/со e os pronomes no instr: The preposition с/со and the pronouns in the instrumental
A variação С / СО. A preposição с (com): The С / СО variation. The preposition с (with) has a spelling variant. С is used before most words: с дру́гом, с ма́мой, с учи́телем. СО is used before words that begin with a hard-to-say cluster of consonants (for example с, ш, ж or в followed by another consonant) and before мн-, and it is also used in the very common со мной (with me): со мной, со стака́ном, со всеми́. Why? Ease of pronunciation again. «С дру́гом» is easy to say. But stacking several consonants in a row (с + мн, с + вс) would be a mouthful, so Russian inserts an -о- as a cushion: со мной. English does something similar with "a" and "an". The personal pronouns in the instrumental. As in the dative, the personal pronouns have special instrumental forms, and you have to learn them. Watch the rule of the "н": when он, она́, оно́, они́ come after a preposition, they get an н- at the start: с ним (with him), с ней (with her), с ни́ми (with them), о нём (about him: prepositional), к нему́ (to him: dative). But when the pronoun does not follow a preposition, there is no н: его́ (his / him, with no preposition), её (her), их (their / them).
Cinco usos principais. (1) Companhia, co: Five main uses. (1) Company, with «с»: «с другом». (2) Instrument or means, WITHOUT a preposition: «писать ручкой», «есть ложкой». (3) Profession with «работать» and «быть»: «Я работаю врачом», «Он хочет быть учителем». (4) Time: «утром, днём, вечером, ночью» and the seasons «зимой, весной, летом, осенью». (5) Place, with the prepositions «над» (above), «под» (under), «перед» (in front of), «за» (behind) and «между» (between), and also «рядом с» (next to): «Лампа стоит над столом».

B Tabelas de apoio: Plural, Adjetivos e: Support tables: plural, adjectives and possessives in the instrumental. Verbs that take the instrumental. Some verbs always take the instrumental. Here are the main ones. Watch the verb быть: in the past and the future it usually takes the instrumental for what someone is. This is one of the most important rules. Notice: быть in the past or future puts the predicate (what the person is) in the instrumental. But быть does not exist in the present (you know that from Lesson 4), so in the present the predicate stays in the nominative: Я студе́нт. (I am a student: no verb, nominative.) Я был студе́нтом. (I was a student: with the verb, instrumental.) English has no case here at all, so the thing to memorise is simply the pattern: was / will be / became + instrumental.

O uso idiomático: мы с X. Aqui está uma: The idiom мы с X. This is one of the most elegant constructions in Russian. When Russian wants to say "X and I", it says "we with X". How to use it: the subject is always мы (we), even when the group is only two people, and the verb is plural. The «с» + instrumental names the other person. Notice what English does: "Eva and I" lists two people with "and". Russian says "we, together with Eva". In place of "my husband and I", Russian says "we with the husband". It is used all the time in daily life.
Eva and I decided to go to Siberia.
My husband and I live in Moscow.
My friend and I are going to the movies.
O instrumental de tempo. Algumas express: The instrumental of time. Some time expressions use the instrumental with no preposition. You have seen this in passing with the prepositional; this is the right place for it. Notice that these adverbs are really instrumental forms of nouns (у́тро → у́тром, день → днём, ве́чер → ве́чером, ночь → но́чью). That is why they count as instrumental. But you do not need to think about that, you only need to use them. English does the same job with "in the" or with no word at all ("mornings", "in summer").
In the morning I drink coffee.

PASSO 1: Os erros que o brasileiro VAI c: STEP 1: The mistakes English speakers WILL make with the instrumental. Mistake 1: using С when it is not needed. Wrong: Я пишу́ с ру́чкой. Right: Я пишу́ ру́чкой. You think "with a pen" and translate it as «с ручкой». But the pen is an extension of the hand, so there is no С: bare instrumental. Mistake 2: leaving out С when it is needed. Wrong: Я иду́ дру́гом. Right: Я иду́ с дру́гом. The friend is another person, not an extension of your body, so С is needed. Mistake 3: using С with tools. Wrong: Я ем суп с ло́жкой. Right: Я ем суп ло́жкой. The spoon is an extension of the hand: bare instrumental. Mistake 4: forgetting that ПОД and ЗА change case. Wrong: Кот под стол (meaning "the cat is under the table"). Right: Кот под столо́м. Place = instrumental. Movement = accusative. Mistake 5: forgetting the С / СО variation. Wrong: Он идёт с мной. Right: Он идёт со мной. Mistake 6: leaving out н- after a preposition. Wrong: Я иду́ с им. Right: Я иду́ с ним. After a preposition, он becomes ним (with н). Mistake 7: not using the instrumental with быть in the past or future. Wrong: Я был студе́нт. Right: Я был студе́нтом. Быть in the past usually puts the predicate in the instrumental. Mistake 8: mixing up быть in the present (nominative) with быть in the past (instrumental). Wrong: Я студе́нтом. (in the present) Right: Я студе́нт (nominative: present). Я был студе́нтом (instrumental: past). Быть does not exist in the present, so the predicate stays in the nominative; only in the past and the future does it go into the instrumental. Mistake 9: forgetting that МЕ́ЖДУ takes the instrumental. Wrong: Ме́жду стол и дива́н. Right: Ме́жду столо́м и дива́ном. Ме́жду takes the instrumental on both sides. Mistake 10: leaving the noun in the nominative where an instrument ending is needed. Wrong: Я пишу́ ру́чка. Right: Я пишу́ ру́чкой. Masculine and neuter: -ОМ/-ЕМ. Feminine in -а: -ОЙ. Feminine in -ь: -ЬЮ. STEP 2: Full sentences with the instrumental. Here are real sentences, so you can see the instrumental at work. STEP 3: Summary table: the instrumental case.

Between the table and the sofa — the lamp.
